correctness.rationale: PASS. For p>2 the half-Hessian of squared l_p norm has exact inverse H_N^-1=(N^(p-2)diag(z_j^(2-p))+(p-2)zz^T/N^2)/(p-1); corresponding weighted Q inverse has diagonal d_j^-p. With m=min d_j>0, M=max d_j, subtracting H_N^-1 from K H_Q^-1 for K=M^p/m^(p-2) gives nonnegative diagonal and nonnegative rank-one terms. Invert Loewner order to obtain H_Q<=K H_N, with equality in the supremum as a coordinate carrying M tends to zero with another coordinate carrying m fixed (also uniform weights). For K<=1, G=N^2-Q^2 is convex and coordinate nondecreasing on the nonnegative orthant; its absolute even extension yields an absolute norm and via block coordinate triangle inequalities, the defect on arbitrary nonzero Banach blocks. K>1 yields negative curvature on the two-block restriction; any positive weight and a zero weight gives explicit small-epsilon midpoint failure since p>2. All zero weights recover original norm. Independent SymPy p=4 two-variable Hessian and four near-axis samples reproduced sharp ratio 0.835918367... for (.8,.7); this is a sanity check, not all-p proof.

This is a mathematically motivated boundary in operator/dilation theory, not a renamed scalar test.
